findings.title: BOLA/IDOR: Archive Another User's Order to Access Receipt Containing Flag
findings.description:
The Trading Platform suffers from a Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) vulnerability across two endpoints: /order/<id>/archive and /order/<id>/receipt.

The application grants read access to an order's receipt if the authenticated user is either the creator OR the archiver of the order. By accessing /order/<id>/archive on an order belonging to another user, an attacker becomes that order's 'archiver' and subsequently gains unauthorized access to the receipt.

Attack chain:
1. Login as test:test (credentials leaked in HTML comment)
2. Enumerate order IDs near own orders (300123, 300214, 300327, 300481)
3. Access GET /order/300198/archive - another user's order is archived under attacker's account
4. Access GET /order/300198/receipt - now accessible because attacker is the 'archiver'
5. Receipt contains the CTF flag.
findings.evidence: FLAG: flag{8b9df79e-91eb-4f4e-8449-5e1d207a0d83} Receipt response for /order/300198/receipt after archiving: flag{8b9df79e-91eb-4f4e-8449-5e1d207a0d83} Order 300198 (belonging to another user) was successfully archived via GET /order/300198/archive returning HTTP 200 with Orders page. Subsequently, /order/300198/receipt returned the receipt with the flag.

reproduction.command:
1. POST / with username=test
2. Follow redirect to /password/test
3. POST /password/test with username=test&user_id=10032&password=test
4. GET /order/300198/archive (with session cookie) -> archives another user's order
5. GET /order/300198/receipt (with session cookie) -> returns receipt with flag
